look_here_first: FIRST, FLIP A ROUND LEAF: the leaf stalk (PETIOLE) enters the UNDERSIDE AWAY FROM THE EDGE (PELTATE), with many veins radiating like an umbrella and scalloped (CRENATE) lobes. THEN FIND THE FLOWER STALK: usually a dense, many-flowered white-green terminal UMBEL-LIKE CLUSTER with many distinct flower stalklets. Whorled pennywort H. verticillata instead usually has clearly separated TIERS of a few flowers along its main stalk. Photograph the entire reproductive axis before assigning species; neither a coin-shaped leaf nor wet habitat alone is enough.

taxonomic_note: Kew POWO accepts Hydrocotyle umbellata L. in Araliaceae; older floras list Apiaceae/Umbelliferae. Published native range includes Texas at STATE level, but the user's BONAP county-zone approval is intentionally not audited here. Do not infer confirmed Hays County nativity from a Texas-level statement or from photographs.

recognition: Perennial low aquatic or damp-ground herb, with creeping underground/ground-level whitish rhizomes or stolons and fibrous roots at the nodes.
Glossy round to slightly broadly scalloped leaves elevated on long upright petioles; petiole joins UNDERSIDE away from leaf edge (peltate), principal veins radiate outward.
Leaves alternate on runner; blade margins CRENATE (shallow rounded scallops) and often shallowly broadly lobed.
Whitish star-like individual flowers are small but numerous, clustered at the top of a separate long leafless stalk in an umbel-like dense terminal head.
Flower cluster usually several to many pedicellate flowers, not several distinctly isolated short whorls up and down the same axis as in H. verticillata.
Mature fruit a small laterally flattened ribbed SCHIZOCARP splitting into two one-seeded mericarps, not the capsule of Dichondra and not an Asteraceae cypsela.
Flowering axis architecture and fruit base/rib detail matter for separating nearly identical water pennyworts, not just the round leaf.
morphology_keys.habit: Rhizomatous perennial that roots freely at nodes, able to form stands in wet soils, ditch margins and shallow water. UT Austin Williamson flora measured foliage/flowering shoots up to about 25 cm tall.
morphology_keys.stem: Creeping underground to shallow exposed horizontal rhizome, often pale white, UT Williamson treatment ~1.2–1.5 mm thick with internodes ~20–60 mm and many adventitious roots at nodes.
morphology_keys.leaf_arrangement: Alternate, arising singly from rhizome nodes; no true opposite leaf pairs.
morphology_keys.leaf: Simple, orbicular/peltate disc with shallow broad crenate lobes (round scallops) and glossy green upper face; UT local 13–63 mm across; 12–16 principal veins radiate from center. Older/younger shoots vary.
morphology_keys.petiole: Long slender upright cylindrical stalk, UT Williamson account ca. 130–260 mm, white at underground base, green aboveground; attaches to lower blade surface not its margin.
morphology_keys.leaf_attachment: PELTATE: junction/umbilicus is on the underside of the blade, toward its center or slightly off center. Compare Dichondra and Centella whose petiole enters an open notch at the outer blade margin.
morphology_keys.flowers: Many tiny bisexual white to greenish-white flowers at the top of a long axillary flowering stalk. Each locally measured individual flower ~3 mm across, 5 separate star-spread petals, 5 stamens, 2 styles, and an inferior ovary. Calyx teeth/sepals absent or minute, DO NOT mislabel green structures as five leafy sepals.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Usually one many-flowered dense terminal, umbel-like cluster (botanical Williamson treatment calls the short densely packed axis a condensed raceme with 30+ helically alternate flowers) on a leafless long peduncle. Each flower on a separate pedicel; clusters ~10–15 mm across locally. A small number of additional tiers is possible: count/spacing across the full axis, not only its apex.
morphology_keys.flowering_stalk: Peduncle commonly similar height to its paired leaf stalk. Pedicels spread out from compressed axis of umbel-like cluster; individually ~4–5.5 mm at anthesis in Williamson treatment, often elongating in fruit.
morphology_keys.fruit: Small dry SCHIZOCARP of two one-seeded D-shaped MERICARPS, laterally flattened, weakly ribbed to clearly ribbed depending on maturity/light; the same UT flora reports individual mericarp ~2 × 1.4–1.6 mm. FNA/GoBotany keys note a conspicuously notched/corrugated basal contour as supporting clue versus H. verticillata. Only claim mm sizes on measured real photographs.
morphology_keys.habitat: Moist lawn depressions, ditches, spring margins, ponds, slow margins of riparian waters, and sandy/organic saturated soils; may grow into shallow water.
morphology_keys.season: Fresh shoots and flowering are favored by adequate moisture and mild/warm weather; timing changes with rainfall, irrigation, drought and frost.
morphology_keys.special_caution: Hydrocotyle umbellata is NOT a composite-headed Asteraceae, not a capsule-bearing Dichondra, and not inherently a single 'water pennywort' species: several wetland Hydrocotyle look nearly identical when sterile.

comparisons.look_here_first: Do TWO quick checks before bothering with species-level pennywort comparisons: (1) does the leaf stalk enter near the CENTER of the underside (peltate) or at the BASE/NOTCH? (2) is the flowering stalk ONE terminal many-flowered spray, or an elongated axis with several spaced whorls/branches?

field_comparison_matrix.reproductive: Dense many-flowered mostly terminal simple umbel-like cluster; pedicellate florets; usually 15–35+ flowers

disambiguation_key.if: Petiole enters underside at blade center or inside margin (peltate), small white flowers in clusters
Peltate AND one crowded upper many-flowered cluster (a few low extra tiers possible)
disambiguation_key.then: Favors Hydrocotyle umbellata; verify mature fruit/whole shoot

disambiguation_key.if: Peltate AND multiple spaced flower tiers along an elongate unbranched axis
Peltate AND long branched primary umbels that bear their own whorled flower lines
Leaf split down almost to petiole at edge, clearly NOT peltate, aquatic/wet
disambiguation_key.then: Consider H. ranunculoides or Centella; check flowers and leaf lobing

disambiguation_key.if: Kidney-shaped, margin entire, pale solitary five-lobed flower
Opposite leaves and tiny yellow composite heads
Opposite leaves and button cluster at end of a stalk

comparisons.species_certainty_warning: Entire flower axis is best for H. umbellata versus H. verticillata. H. umbellata may have additional whorls and H. verticillata may have crowded terminal whorls; base of ripe fruits plus full flowering stalk should resolve borderline specimens. Do not force ID from sterile leaf.

family_genus_teaching.family: Current Kew places Hydrocotyle within ARALIACEAE (order Apiales), a historical member of Apiaceae/Umbelliferae in older manuals. Its fruit splits into two dry one-seeded MERICARPS; the whitish tiny flowers each have five petals and stamens, not Asteraceae florets.
family_genus_teaching.genus: Hydrocotyle wetland creepers root at nodes; local H. umbellata and H. verticillata both have long-petioled, round PELTATE blades. Cluster arrangement, not a single leaf, separates them.
family_genus_teaching.species: Hydrocotyle umbellata usually has a dense terminal group of many pedicellate five-petal flowers, fruit flattened and two-part. Contrast H. verticillata with spaced small whorls on the flowering stalk.
family_genus_teaching.crew_prompt: Flip one leaf and show exactly where its petiole meets the underside; then photograph the WHOLE flowering axis, not only the top white cluster.

ecological_notes.habitat: Wet/marshy ground, spring/stream edges, pond margins, low irrigation depressions and shallow floating mats. Locally appropriate planting needs actual wet habitat and verified provenance.
ecological_notes.regional_range: Kew POWO confirms Texas as state-level native; current project county/target-zone BONAP decision remains intentionally unverified.
ecological_notes.management: Rhizomatous water/edge vegetation can spread rapidly where consistently wet. Do not treat a native-looking wetland carpet as confirmed native or problematic without species and local restoration goals.
ecological_notes.ecological_relationships: Wetland cover can provide aquatic edge complexity; no invented Lepidoptera larval-host or specialty bee numerical counts. Link to dashboards only if verifiable species-level numbers exist.
